There will be some way or other a mighty struggle8 between Satan's kingdom and the church, and probably all ways of opposition that can be; and doubtless great opposition by external force wherein the princes of the world that are on the devil's side shall join hand in hand, for 'tis said, "The kings of the earth are gathered together to battle."9 Revelation 19:19 ["And I saw the beast, and the kings of the earth, and their armies, gathered together to make

-- 464 --

war against him that sat on the horse, and against his army"]. And probably withal there will be great opposition of subtile disputers, and carnal reasoning, and great persecution in many places, and great opposition by virulent reproaches, and also great opposition by craft and subtilty. That devil now doubtless will ply his skill as well as strength to the utmost. The devils and those that belong to his kingdom will everywhere be stirred up, and engaged to make united and violent opposition against this holy religion that they see prevailing so mightily in the world. But,

3.1 Christ and his church shall in this battle obtain a complete and entire victory over their enemies; they shall be totally routed and overthrown in this their last effort. When the powers of hell and earth are thus gathered together against Christ, Christ and his armies shall come forth against them by his word and2 Spirit to fight with them.3 In how august and glorious a manner is this coming forth of Christ and his church to this battle described in the Revelation 19, beginning with the Revelation 19:11 ["And I saw heaven opened, and behold a white horse; and he that sat upon him was called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he doth judge and make war"]. And to represent to us how great the victory should be that they should obtain, and how mighty the overthrow of their enemies, 'tis said in the Revelation 19:17 ["all the fowls … of heaven, … gather yourselves together unto the supper of the great God; that ye may eat the flesh of kings, and the flesh of captains, and the flesh of mighty men"]. And then in the following verses we have an account of the victory and overthrow ["And the beast was taken, and with him the false prophet … and them that worshipped his image. These both were cast alive into a lake of fire burning with brimstone. And the remnant were slain with the sword of him that sat upon the horse … and all the fowls were filled with their flesh"].4

In this victory the seventh vial shall be poured out. It is said, Revelation 16:16, of the great army that should be gathered together against Christ, "And he gathered them together into a place called in the Hebrew tongue Armageddon"; and then it is said, "And the seventh angel poured out his vial5 into the

-- 465 --

air; and there came a great voice out of the temple of heaven, from the throne, saying, It is done."6 Now the business is done for Satan and his adherents; when this victory is obtained all is in effect done. Satan's last and greatest opposition is conquered; all his measures are broke, the pillars of his kingdom are fragments in sunder and will fall of course. The devil is utterly baffled and confounded, and knows not what else to do; he now sees his Antichristian and Mohammedan and heathenish kingdoms through the world all tumbling about his ears. He and his most powerful instruments are now taken captives. Now that is in effect done that the church of God had been so long waiting for, and hoping for, and so earnestly crying to God for, saying, "How long, Lord, holy and true?"7 Now the time is come.

The angel8 that set his right foot on the sea [and his left foot on the earth] lift up his hand to heaven and swore by him that liveth [for ever and ever] who created heaven and all things that are9 therein, and the earth and the things that therein are, and the sea and the things that are therein, that when the seventh angel come to sound, the time should be no longer. And now the time is coming, now the seventh trumpet sounds, and the seventh vial are poured out, both together intimating that now all is finished as to the overthrow of Satan's visible kingdom on earth.

This victory shall be far the greatest that ever was obtained over Satan and his adherents. By this blow with which the stone cut out of the mountain without hands shall strike the image of gold and silver and brass and iron and clay, it shall all be broken in pieces; this will be a finishing blow to the image so that it shall become the chaff of the summer threshing floor.1 It shall be with a glorious manifestation of divine power. Christ shall therein especially appear2 in the character of "King of Kings, and Lord of Lords," as Revelation 19:16. Now Christ shall dash his enemies, even the strongest and proudest of them, in pieces as a potter's vessel; and they shall be broken all in

-- 466 --

shivers.3 Then shall strength be shown out of weakness,4 and Christ shall cause his church, as it were, to thresh the mountains, as Isaiah 41:15–16, "Behold, I will make thee a new sharp threshing instrument having teeth: and thou shalt thresh the mountains, and beat them small, and make the hills as chaff." And then shall be fulfilled that in Isaiah 41:13–15 ["For I the Lord thy God will hold thy right hand … I will help thee. Fear not.… Behold, I will make thee a new sharp threshing instrument"].5

4.6 Consequent on this victory, Satan's visible kingdom on earth shall be destroyed. When Satan is conquered in this last battle, the church7 of Christ shall have easy work of it, as Joshua and the children [of Israel] had obtained that great victory over the five kings of the Amorites when the sun stood still, and God sent great hail stones ‹on their enemies›8 they after that went to one city and another and burnt them with fire.9 They had easy work of subduing the cities and country they belonged to. So it was also after that other great battle that Joshua had with that great multitude at the waters of Merom.1 So after this glorious victory of Christ and his church over their enemies, over the chief powers of Satan's kingdom, they shall destroy that kingdom in all those cities and country they belonged to. After this victory, the word of God shall have a speedy and swift progress through the earth, as it is said that on the pouring out of the seventh vial, "the cities of the nations fell, and every island fled away, and the mountains were not found," Revelation 16:19–20.2 When once the stone cut out [of the mountain without hands]3 had broken the image in pieces,

-- 467 --

it was easy to abolish all remains of it; the very wind will carry it away as the chaff of the summer threshing4 floor. Because Satan's visible kingdom on earth shall now be destroyed, therefore 'tis said that the seventh vial by which this be done shall be poured out into the air,5 which is represented in Scripture as the special seat of his kingdom, for he is called the prince of the power of the air, Ephesians 2:2. Now is come the time for punishing leviathan, that piercing serpent of which we read, Isaiah 27:1, "In that day the Lord with his sore and great and strong sword shall punish leviathan the piercing serpent, even leviathan that crooked serpent; he shall slay the dragon that is in the sea."

Concerning this overthrow of Satan's visible kingdom on earth I would, 1. show wherein this overthrow of Satan's visible kingdom shall chiefly consist, 2. the extent and universality of this overthrow.

1.6 I would show wherein this overthrow of ‹Satan's kingdom› shall chiefly consist. I shall mention the particular things that it shall consist of without pretending to determine7 in what order they shall come to pass, or which shall be accomplished first, or whether they shall be accomplished together.8

91.1 Heresies and infidelity and superstition among those that have been brought up under the light of the gospel will then be abolished: [an] end to Socinianism and Arianism and Quakerism and Arminianism. Deism that is now so bold shall be crushed and driven away and vanish to nothing. And all shall agree in the sure, great and important doctrines of the gospel, agreeable to that in Zechariah 14:9, "And the Lord shall be king over all the earth: in that day shall there be one Lord, and his name one."2 [Then shall be] abolished all superstitious ways of worship; [all] shall agree in worshipping God in his own way, Jeremiah 32:39, "And I will give them one heart, and one way, that they may fear me for ever, for the good of them, and their children after them."

-- 468 --

32.4 The kingdom of Antichrist shall be utterly overthrown. His kingdom and dominion has been much brought down already by the vial poured out on his throne in the Reformation;5 but then it shall be utterly destroyed. Then shall it be proclaimed, "Babylon is fallen, is fallen."6 When the seventh angel sounds, "the time, times, and half"7 shall be out, "and the time shall be no longer."8 Then shall be accomplished concerning Antichrist the things that are written in the Revelation 18, of the spiritual Babylon, that great city Rome, or the idolatrous Roman government that has for so many ages been the great enemy of the Christian church, first under heathenism and then under popery; that proud city that lifted herself up to heaven, and above God himself in her pride and haughtiness, that cruel bloody city9 shall come down to the ground. Then shall that be fulfilled, Isaiah 26:5, "For he bringeth down them that dwell on high; the lofty city, he layeth it low; he layeth it low, even to the ground; he bringeth it even to the dust." She shall be thrown down with violence, "like a great millstone cast into the sea," and "shall be found no more" at all, and shall become an "habitation of devils, and the hold of every foul spirit, and a cage of every unclean and hateful bird."1 Now shall she be stripped of all her glory, and riches, and ornaments, and shall be cast out as an abominable branch,2 and shall be "trodden down as the mire of the streets."3 All her policy and craft that she so abounded in shall not save her. And God will make his people that have been so persecuted by her to come and put their foot on the neck of Antichrist;4 and he shall be their footstool.5 All strength and wisdom of this great whore shall fail her, and there shall be none to help her; the kings of the earth that before gave their power and strength6 [to] the beast shall now "hate the whore, and

-- 469 --

shall make [her desolate and naked, and shall eat her flesh, and burn her with fire]," Revelation 17:16.

3.7 That other great kingdom that Satan has set up in opposition to the Christian church, viz. his Mohammedan kingdom, shall be utterly overthrown. The locusts and horsemen in the Revelation 9 have their appointed and limited time set them there, and the false prophet shall be taken and destroyed.8 And then, though Mohammedanism has been so vastly propagated in the world, and is upheld by such great empire, this smoke that has ascended out of the bottomless pit shall be utterly scattered before the light of that glorious day, and the Mohammedan empire shall fall at the sound of the great trumpet that then shall be blown.9

4.1 Jewish infidelity shall then be overthrown. However obstinate they have now been for above seventeen hundred years in their rejecting Christ, and instances of conversion of any of2 that nation have been so very rare ever since the destruction of Jerusalem, but they have against the plain teachings of their own prophets continued to approve of the cruelty of their forefathers in crucifying [Christ]; yet when this day comes the thick veil that blinds their eyes shall be removed, 2 Corinthians 3:16, and divine grace shall melt and renew their hard hearts, "And they shall look on him whom they [have pierced, and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son, and shall be in bitterness for him, as one that is in bitterness for his firstborn]," Zechariah 12:10 etc.3 And then shall all Israel be saved.4 The Jews in all their dispersions shall cast away their old infidelity, and shall wonderfully have their hearts changed, and abhor themselves for their past unbelief and obstinacy; and shall flow together to the blessed Jesus, penitently, humbly, and joyfully owning him as their glorious king and only savior, and shall with all their hearts as with one heart and voice declare his praises unto other nations.5

Nothing is more certainly foretold than this national conversion of the Jews is in the Romans 116 Romans 11. And there are also

-- 470 --

many passages of the Old Testament that can't be interpreted in any other sense, that I can't now stand to mention. Besides the prophecies of the calling of the Jews, we have a remarkable seal of the fulfillment of this great event in providence by a thing that is a kind of continual miracle, viz. the preserving them a distinct [nation] when in such a dispersed condition for above sixteen hundred years. The world affords nothing else like it—a remarkable hand of providence. When they shall be called, then shall that ancient people that were alone God's people for so long a time be God's people again, never to be rejected more, one fold with the Gentiles; and then also shall the remains of the ten tribes wherever they are, and though they have been rejected much longer than [the Jews], be brought in with their brethren, the Jews. The prophecies of Hosea especially seem to hold this forth, that in the future glorious times of the church both Judah and Ephraim, or Judah7 and the ten tribes, shall be brought in together, and shall be united as one people as they formerly were under David and Solomon, as Hosea 1:11, and so in the last chapter of Hosea, and other parts of his prophecy.8

Though we don't know the time in which this conversion of the nation of Israel will come to pass, yet this much we may determine by Scripture, that it will [be] before [the] glory of the Gentile part of the church shall be fully accomplished, because it is said that their coming in shall be life from the dead to the Gentiles, Romans 11:12, Romans 11:15 ["Now if the fall of them be the riches of the world … how much more their fulness? … For if the casting away of them be the reconciling of the world, what shall the receiving of them be, but life from the dead?"].

-- 471 --

1SERMON TWENTY-SEVEN2
[For the moth shall eat them up like a garment, and the worm shall eat them like wool: but my righteousness shall be for ever, and my salvation from generation to generation.] Isaiah 51:8
[DOCTRINE]
[The Work of Redemption is a work that God carries on from the fall of man to the end of the world.]

5.3 Then shall also Satan's heathenish kingdom be overthrown. Gross heathenism now possesses great part of the earth, and there are supposed to be more heathens now in the world than of all professions put together, Jews, Mohammedans and Christians. But then the heathen nations shall be enlightened with the glorious gospel.4 There will be a5 wonderful spirit of pity towards them, and zeal for their instruction and conversion put into multitudes, and many shall go forth and carry the gospel unto them. And then shall the joyful sound be heard among them, and the sun of righteousness shall then arise, with his glorious light shining on those many vast regions of the earth that have been covered with heathenish darkness for many thousand years, many of them doubtless ever since the times of Moses and Abraham, and have lain thus long in a miserable condition under the cruel tyranny of the devil, that has all this while blinded and befooled them, and domineered over them, and made a prey of them from

-- 472 --

generation to generation. Now the glad tidings of the gospel shall be proclaimed among them, the joyful trumpet shall sound there, and they shall be brought out of darkness into marvelous light.

It is promised that heathenism shall thus be destroyed in many places. God has6 said it, that "the gods that han't made these heavens [and the earth, even they shall perish from the earth, and from under these heavens]," Jeremiah 10:11, and that he will utterly abolish idols Isaiah 2:18. Then shall the many nations of Africa, the nations of Negroes and others—heathens that chiefly fill that quarter of the world, that now seem to be in a state but little above the beasts in many respects and as much below them in many others7—be enlightened with glorious light, and delivered from all their darkness, and shall become a civil, Christian and an understanding and holy people. Then shall this vast continent of America, that now in so great part of it is covered with barbarous ignorance and cruelty, be everywhere covered with glorious gospel light and Christian love, and instead of worshipping the devil as now, they now shall serve the true God and praises shall be sung to the Lord Jesus Christ, the blessed savior of the world, everywhere. So may we expect it will be in that great and populous part of the world, the East Indies that are now mostly worshippers of the devil, and so throughout8 that vast country, cruel Turkey. And then the kingdom of Christ will be also established in those continents that have more lately been discovered towards the north and south poles, where now men differ very little from the wild beasts—excepting that they worship the devil and beasts do not—and in many countries that never yet have been discovered.9 Thus will be gloriously fulfilled that in the Isaiah 35:1 ["The wilderness and the solitary place shall be glad for them; and the desert shall rejoice, and blossom as the rose"], and verses six and seven ["in the wilderness shall waters break out, and streams in the desert. And the parched ground shall become a pool, and the thirsty land springs of water"].

Having thus shown wherein this overthrow of Satan's visible kingdom consists, I come now to the second thing1 to be observed concerning

-- 473 --

it, viz. its universal extent. The visible kingdom of Satan shall be overthrown and the kingdom of Christ set up on the ruins of it everywhere, throughout the whole habitable globe. Now shall the promise made to Abraham be fulfilled, that "In him and in his seed all the families [of the earth shall be blessed]."2 And Christ now shall become the desire of all nations, agreeable to Haggai 2:7.3

Now the kingdom of Christ shall in the most strict and literal sense extend to all nations and the whole earth. There are many passages of Scripture that can be understood in no other sense. What can be more universal than that in Isaiah 11:9, "For the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord, as the waters cover the sea," as much as to say, as there is no part of the channel or cavity of sea anywhere but that4 is covered with water, so there shall be no part of the world of mankind but that shall be covered with the knowledge of God. So it is foretold in the Isaiah 45:22, that all the ends of the earth shall look to Christ and be saved. And to show that these words are to be understood in the most universal sense, it is said in the next verse, "I have sworn by my self, the word is gone out of my mouth …, and shall not return, That unto me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear."5 So the most universal expression is used, Dan. 7.27, "And the kingdom and dominion, and the greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven, shall be given

-- 474 --

to the people of the saints of the most High God":6 all under the whole heaven.7

When the devil was cast out of the Roman empire because that was the highest and principal part of the world and the other nations that were left were low and mean in comparison of them, it was represented as Satan's being cast out of heaven to the earth, Revelation 12:9. But now 'tis represented8 as though he should be cast out of the earth too, and shut up in hell, Revelation 20:1–3 ["And I saw an angel … having the key of the bottomless pit.… And he laid hold on the dragon … and Satan, and bound him a thousand years, And cast him into the bottomless pit, and shut him up … that he should deceive the nations no more, till the thousand years should be fulfilled"].9 This is the greatest revolution by far that ever came to pass; therefore it is said in [the] Romans 16:17–18, that on the pouring out of the seventh vial "there was a great earthquake, such as was not since men were upon earth, so mighty an earthquake, and so great."

And this is the third great dispensation of providence that is in Scripture compared to Christ's coming to judgment. So it is in Revelation 16:15. There after the sixth vial, after the devil's armies were gathered together to their great battle, and just before Christ's glorious victory over them, "Behold,1 I come quickly. Blessed is he that watcheth, and keepeth his garments."2 So it is called Christ's coming in the 2 Thessalonians 2:8. Speaking of Antichrist, it is said, "And then shall that Wicked be revealed, whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit

-- 475 --

of his mouth, and shall destroy with the brightness of his coming." So Christ's coming to set up his kingdom on earth made heaven as 'tis here expressed.3 And to destroy Antichrist is called his coming with "clouds of heaven" to judgment. And this is more like Christ's last coming to judgment than any of the preceding dispensations that are so called on these accounts.

1.4 That the dispensation is so much greater and more universal, and so more like the day of judgment that respects the whole world.

25 On the account of the great spiritual resurrection there will be of the church of God accompanying [it] more resembling the general resurrection at the end of the world than any other. This spiritual resurrection is the resurrection spoken of as attended with judgment, Revelation 20:4 ["And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them: and I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus"].

63.7 Because of the terrible judgments and fearful destruction which shall now be executed on God's enemies, there will doubtless at the introducing of this dispensation be a visible and awful hand of God against blasphemers, deists, and obstinate heretics, and other enemies of Christ, terribly destroying them with remarkable tokens of wrath and vengeance. And especially will that dispensation be attended with terrible judgments on Antichrist. And the cruel persecutors that belong to the church of Rome shall in a most awful manner be destroyed, which is compared to a casting Antichrist into the burning flame in Daniel 7:11, and casting him alive into the lake that burns with fire and brimstone, Revelation 19:20. Then shall this cruel persecuting church suffer those judgments from God that shall be far more dreadful than her cruelest persecutions of the saints, agreeable to Revelation 18:6–7 ["Reward her even as she rewarded you, and double unto her double according to her works.… How much she hath glorified herself … so much torment and sorrow give her"]. The judgments of God that he8 shall execute on the enemies of the church are so great that they are compared to God's sending great

-- 476 --

hailstones from heaven upon them, every one of the weight of a talent, as 'tis said on the pouring out of the seventh vial, Revelation 16:21, "And there fell upon [men] a great hail out of heaven, every stone about the weight of a talent: and men blasphemed God because of the plague of the hail; for the plague thereof was exceeding great."9 And now shall be that treading of the wine press spoken of, Revelation 14:19–20 ["And the angel thrust in his sickle into the earth, and gathered the vine of the earth, and cast it into the great winepress of the wrath of God. And the winepress was trodden without the city, and blood came out of the winepress"].

4.1 This shall put an end to the church's suffering state, and shall be attended with their glorious and joyful praises. The church's afflicted state is long being continued,2 excepting some short intermissions from Christ's resurrection to this time, but now shall be a final end to her suffering state. Indeed after this, near the end of the world, the church shall be greatly threatened; but 'tis said it shall be but for a little season, Revelation 20:3.3 For as the times of the church's rest are but short4 before the long day of her afflictions are at an end, so whatever afflictions she may suffer after this it will be very short. But otherwise the day of the church's affliction and persecution shall now come to a final end.5 The Scripture in many places speaks of this time as the end of the church's suffering state.6 And so Isaiah 51:22, God says to his church at this time, "Behold, I have taken out of thine hand the cup of trembling, even the dregs of the cup of my fury; thou shalt no more drink it again." Then shall that be proclaimed to the church, Isaiah 40:1–2, "Comfort ye, [comfort ye my people, saith your God]. Speak ye comfortably to Jerusalem, [and] cry unto her, that her warfare7 is accomplished, [that her iniquity is pardoned: for she hath received of the Lord's hand double for all her sins]." Also

-- 477 --

that in the Isaiah 54:8–9, belongs to this time ["I hid my face from thee for a moment; but with everlasting kindness will I have mercy on thee.… So have I sworn that I would not be wroth with thee, nor rebuke thee"]. And so Isaiah 60:20,8 "The Lord shall be thine everlasting light, and the days of thy mourning shall be ended." And so Zephaniah 3:15, "The Lord hath taken away thy judgments, he hath cast out thine enemy: the king of Israel, even the Lord, is in the midst of thee: thou shalt not see evil any more."

The time that had been before this has been the church's sowing time, wherein she sowed in tears and in blood; but now is her harvest, wherein she will come again, rejoicing, bringing her sheaves with her.9 Now the time of the travail of the woman clothed with the sun is at an end, now she has brought forth her son;1 for this glorious setting up the kingdom of Christ through the world is what the church had been in travail for, with such terrible pangs, for so many ages, Isaiah 26:17, 2 "Like as a woman with child, that draweth near the time of her delivery, is in pain, and crieth out in her pangs; so have we been in thy sight, O Lord."3 And now the church shall forget her sorrows, since a man child is born into the world; now succeeds her joyful praise and triumph.4 These praises shall go up to God then from all parts of the earth, as Isaiah 42:10–12 ["Sing unto the Lord a new song, and his praise from the end of the earth.… Let the wilderness and the cities thereof lift up their voice.… Let them give glory unto the Lord, and declare his praise in the islands"].

And praise shall not only fill the earth but also heaven. The church on earth and the church in heaven shall both gloriously rejoice and praise God as with one heart on that occasion. Without doubt then it will be a time of very distinguishing5 joy and praise among the holy prophets and apostles and other saints in heaven, Revelation 18:20, "Rejoice over her, thou heaven, and ye holy apostles and prophets; for God

-- 478 --

hath6 avenged you of her." See how universal these praises will be in Isaiah 44:23, "Sing, O ye heavens; for the Lord hath done it: shout, ye lower parts of the earth; break forth into singing, ye mountains, O forest, and every tree therein: For the Lord hath redeemed Jacob and glorified himself in Israel." See what joyful praises are sung to God on this occasion by the universal church in heaven and earth in the beginning of the Revelation 19 ["And I heard as it were the voice of a great multitude … saying, Alleluia.… Let us be glad and rejoice, and give honour to him"].7

5.8 This dispensation is above all preceding ones like Christ's coming to judgment in that it so puts an end to the former state of the world and introduces the everlasting kingdom of Christ. Now Satan's visible kingdom shall be overthrown after it had stood ever since the building of Babel. And the old heavens and the old earth shall in a greater measure be passed9 away than ever before, and the new heavens and new earth set up in a far more glorious manner than ever before.1

Thus I have shown how the success of Christ's purchase has been carried on through the times of the afflicted state of the Christian church, from Christ's resurrection till Antichrist is fallen and Satan's visible kingdom on earth is overthrown.2 [I come now,]

-- 479 --

Secondly,3 to show how the success ‹of redemption will be carried on› through that space wherein the Christian church shall for the most part [be] in a state of peace and prosperity.4 And in order to this I would 1. speak of the prosperous state of the church through the bigger part of this period, and 2. of the great apostasy there shall be towards the close of it, and how greatly then the church shall be threatened by her enemies for a short time.

I.5 I would speak of the prosperous state of the church through the bigger part of this period. And in doing this, 1. I would describe this state of the church, and 2. say something of its duration.

1.6 I would describe the prosperous state the, church shall be in.7 And in the general I would observe two things:

1.8 That this is most properly the time of the kingdom of heaven upon earth, though the kingdom of heaven was in a degree set up soon after Christ's resurrection, and in a further degree in Constantine's time, and the Christian church in all ages of it is called the kingdom of heaven; yet this time that we are upon is the principal time of the kingdom of heaven on earth principally intended by the prophecies of Daniel that speak of the kingdom of heaven, whence the Jews took [the name, the kingdom of heaven].9

2.1 Now is the principal fulfillment of all the prophecies of the Old Testament that speak of the glorious times of the gospel that shall be in the latter days. Though [there has been a] glorious fulfillment [of those prophecies] before, yet the2 expressions used are most of them too high for any other time. This is most properly the glorious gospel

-- 480 --

day. Other times are only forerunners and preparatories to this; other times were the seed time but this is the harvest. But more particularly,

31.4 It will be a time of great light and knowledge. The present days are days of darkness in comparison of those days. The light of that glorious time shall be so great that 'tis represented as though there should then be no night but only day, no evening nor darkness.5 So6 Zechariah 14:6–7 ["And it shall come to pass in that day, that the light shall not be clear, nor dark: But it shall be one day which shall be known to the Lord, not day, nor night: but it shall come to pass, that at evening time it shall be light"]. 'Tis further represented as though God would then give such light to his church, that should so much exceed the glory of the light of the light of the sun and moon, that they should be ashamed, Isaiah 24:23, "Then the moon shall be confounded, and the sun ashamed, when the Lord of hosts shall reign in Mount Zion, [and in Jerusalem, and] before his [ancients gloriously]."

There is a kind of a veil now cast over the bigger part of the world that keeps 'em in darkness; but then this veil shall be destroyed, Isaiah 25:7, "And he will destroy in this mountain the face of the covering cast over all people, and the veil that is spread over all nations." And then all countries and nations, even those that are now most ignorant, shall be full of light and knowledge. Great knowledge shall prevail everywhere. It may be hoped that then many of the Negroes and Indians will be divines, and that excellent books will be published in Africa, in Ethiopia, in Turkey—and not only very learned men, but others that are more ordinary men, shall then be very knowing in religion, Isaiah 32:3–4, "The eyes of them that see shall7 not be dim, and the ears [of them that hear shall hearken]. The heart also of the rash shall understand knowledge."8 Knowledge then shall be very universal among all sorts of persons, agreeable to Jeremiah 31:34, "And they shall teach no more every man his neighbor, and every man his brother, [saying, Know the Lord: for they shall all know me, from the least of them unto the greatest of them]."

There shall then be a wonderful unraveling the difficulties in the

-- 481 --

doctrines of religion, and clearing up seeming inconsistencies; "so crooked things shall be made straight, and rough places shall be made plain," and darkness shall become light before God's people.9 Difficulties in Scripture shall then be cleared up, and wonderful things shall be discovered in the word of God that were never discovered before. The great discovery of those things in religion that had been1 before kept hid seems to [be] compared to removing the veiling and discovering the ark of the testimony to the people that2 used to be kept in the secret of the temple and never seen by them. Thus at the sounding of the seventh angel, when 'tis proclaimed "that the kingdoms of this world [are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Christ],"3 'tis added that, "the temple of God was opened in heaven, and there was seen in his temple the ark of his testament."4 So great shall be the increase of knowledge in this time that heaven shall be, as it were, opened to the church of God on earth.

2.5 It shall be a time of great holiness; now vital religion shall everywhere prevail and reign. Religion shall not be an empty profession as it now mostly is, but holiness of heart and life shall abundantly prevail. Those times shall be an exception from what Christ says of the ordinary state of the church, viz. that there shall be but6 few [saved],7 for now holiness shall become general, Isaiah 60:21, 8 "Thy people also shall be all righteous." Not that there will be none remaining in a Christianless condition, but that visible wickedness shall be suppressed everywhere, and true holiness shall become general, though not universal. And it shall be a wonderful time, not only for the multitude of godly men, but for eminency of grace, Isaiah 65:20, "There shall be no more thence an infant of days, [nor an old man that hath not filled his days: for the child shall die an hundred years old; but the sinner being an hundred years old shall be accursed]." And Zechariah 12:8, "He that is feeble among them at that day shall be as David; and the house of David shall be as God, as the angel of the

-- 482 --

Lord before them." And holiness shall then be, as it were, inscribed on everything, on all men's common business and employments, and the common utensils of life, all shall be, as it were, dedicated to God and improved for holy purposes; everything shall then be done to the glory of God, Isaiah 23:18, "And her merchandise and her hire shall be holiness to the Lord." And so Zechariah 14:20–21 ["In that day shall there be upon the bells of the horses, HOLINESS UNTO THE LORD.… Yea, every pot in Jerusalem and in Judah shall be holiness unto the Lord"].9 And so God's people then, as they shall be eminent for holiness of heart, so they shall also be for holiness of life and practice.

3.1 It shall be a time wherein religion shall in every respect be uppermost in the world. It shall be had in great esteem and honor. The saints have hitherto for the most part been kept under, and wicked men have governed; but now they will be uppermost. The kingdom "shall be given into the hands of the saints of the most High" God, Daniel 7:27. And they "shall reign on earth," Revelation 5:10, "And hast made us unto our God kings." [They]2 shall live and reign with Christ [a thousand years], Revelation 20:4. [In that day] such persons shall be chiefly promoted. Vital religion then shall take the possession of kings' palaces and thrones, and those that [are] in highest advancement shall generally be holy men, Isaiah 49:23, "And kings shall be thy nursing fathers, [and their queens thy nursing mothers]." Kings shall then improve all their power and glory and riches for the advancement3 of the honor and glory of Christ and the good of his church, Isaiah 60:16, "Thou shalt also suck the milk of the Gentiles, and shalt suck the breasts of kings." And the great men of the world, the rich merchants and others that have great wealth and influence, shall devote all to Christ and his church, Psalms 45:12, "The daughter of Tyre shall be there with a gift; … the rich among the people shall intreat thy favor."

4.4 These will be times of great peace and love. There shall then be universal peace and good understanding among all the nations of the world, instead of such confusion, wars, and bloodshed as has hitherto been from one age to another, Isaiah 2:4, "And he shall judge

-- 483 --

among the nations, and [shall] rebuke many people: and they shall beat [their swords into ploughshares, and their spears into pruning-hooks: nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more]." So it is represented as if all instruments of war should be destroyed as having become useless, in Psalms 46:9, 5 "He maketh wars to cease to the ends of the earth; he breaketh the bow, and cutteth the spear in sunder; and burneth the chariot in the fire."6 Then shall all nations dwell quietly and safely without the fear of any enemy; Isaiah 32:18, "And my people shall dwell in a peaceable habitation, and in sure dwellings, and in quiet resting places."7 And then shall malice and envy and wrath and revenge be suppressed everywhere, and peace and love shall prevail between one man and another. Which is most elegantly set forth in the Isaiah 11:6–9 ["The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb … and a little child shall lead them. And the cow and the bear shall feed.… And the sucking child shall play on the hole of the asp.… They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain. For the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord"]. Then shall there be peace and love between rulers and ruled. Rulers shall love their people, and with all their might seek their best good; and the people shall love their rulers, and shall joyfully submit to them, and give 'em that honor that is their due. And so shall there be an happy love and peace everywhere between ministers8 and people, Malachi 4:6, "[And he shall] turn the heart of [the] fathers to the children, [and the heart of the children to their fathers]." Then shall flourish in an eminent manner those Christian virtues of meekness, forgiveness, long-suffering, gentleness, goodness, brotherly kindness, those excellent fruits of the Spirit.9 Men in their temper and disposition shall then be like the lamb of God, the lovely Jesus. The body shall be conformed to the head.1

And then shall all the world be united in peace and love in one amiable society; all nations, in all parts, on every side of the globe, shall then be knit together in sweet harmony, all parts of God's church assisting and promoting the knowledge and spiritual good one of

-- 484 --

another. A communication shall be then upheld between all parts of the world to that end, and the art of navigation that is now improved so much in fear, with covetousness2 and pride, and is used so much by wicked, debauched men, shall then be consecrated to God, and improved for holy uses, as we read in the Isaiah 60:5 ["the abundance of the sea shall be converted unto thee"], Isaiah 60:9, ["Surely the isles shall wait for me, and the ships of Tarshish … to bring thy sons from far"]. And it shall then be a time wherein men will be abundant in expressing their love one to another, not only in words but in deeds of charity, as we learn, Isaiah 32:5, and "the vile person shall no more be called liberal, nor the churl be said to be bountiful" and Isaiah 32:8, "But the liberal deviseth liberal things; and by liberal things shall he stand."

5.3 A time of excellent order in the church discipline and government [shall]4 be settled in his church; all the world [shall then be] as one church, one orderly, regular, beautiful society, one body, all the members in beautiful proportion.5 Then [shall] that [be] verified [in] Psalms 122:3, 6 "Jerusalem is builded7 as a city compact together."

6.8 [The] church of God shall be beautiful and glorious on these accounts, [yea it will appear in] perfection of beauty, Isaiah 60:1, "Arise, shine; [for thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee]." And Isaiah 61:10 ["He hath covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decketh himself with ornaments, and as a bride adorneth herself with her jewels"]. As a bride adorned for her husband,9 [the church will then be] the greatest image of heaven.

7.1 [That will be a time] of great temporal [prosperity]. [Such a] spiritual state [will] have a natural tendency to it: to health, Zechariah 8:4; ease,2 quietness, pleasantness, wealth, great increase of children, Zechariah 8:5. Through the remarkable blessing of heaven, Isaiah 65:21, "[They shall] build houses, [and inhabit them; and they shall] plant

-- 485 --

vineyards, [and eat the fruit of them]."3 Elsewhere: [Micah 4:4, "But they shall sit every man] under his vine and under his fig tree; [and none shall make them afraid]"; Zechariah 8:12; Jeremiah 31:12–13 ["Therefore they shall come and sing in the height of Zion, and shall flow together to the goodness of the Lord, for wheat, and for wine …; and they shall not sorrow any more at all. Then shall the virgin rejoice in the dance …: for I will turn their mourning into joy"];4 and Amos 9:13 ["Behold, the days come … that the plowman shall overtake the reaper … and the mountains shall drop sweet wine, and all the hills shall melt"].5 [Then they shall receive] all manner of tokens of God's presence, and acceptance, and favor, Jeremiah 33:9. [They shall] call on God, and he will answer.6 [The] days of Solomon [were] but an image of those days.

78.8 [It shall also be a] time of great rejoicing: Isaiah 35:10, "[And the] ransomed of the Lord [shall] return, [and come to Zion with songs and] everlasting joy [upon their heads: they shall obtain joy and gladness, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away]"; Isaiah 55:12, "For ye shall go out with joy, and be led forth with peace: [the] mountains and [the] hills shall break forth before you into singing"; Isaiah 66:11, "[That ye may suck, and be satisfied with the breasts of her consolations; that ye may] milk out, and be delighted with the abundance of her glory"; Isaiah 12:3, "With joy [shall ye] draw water [out of the wells of salvation]." [This shall be] a time of feasting, the church's glorious wedding day so far as her wedding with Christ shall ever be on earth: Revelation 19:7, "Let us be glad and rejoice [and give honour to him: for the marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife hath made herself ready]"; Revelation 19:9, "Blessed is he that shall be called to the marriage supper [of the Lamb]."9

Secondly,1 [I will speak briefly of the] duration [of the prosperous state of the church. It will be] a long time, Revelation 20:4, "[And I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus … and

-- 486 --

they lived and reigned with Christ] a thousand years"; Isaiah 60:15, 2 "[Whereas thou hast been forsaken and hated, so that no man went through thee, I will make thee an eternal excellency, a] joy of many generations."3

And now let us once more take a view of that building of God.4

-- 487 --

1No. 12: SERMON TWENTY-EIGHT Aug. 17392
[For the moth shall eat them up like a garment, and the worm shall eat them like wool: but my righteousness shall be for ever, and my salvation from generation to generation.] Isaiah 51:8
DOCTRINE
[The Work of Redemption is a work that God carries on from the fall of man to the end of the world.]
PROPOSITION
[That the space of time from the end of Christ's humiliation to the end of the world is all taken up in bringing about the great effect or success of Christ's purchase.]

HAVING shown how the success of Christ's purchase was carried on through the first afflicted state of the church, we come in the second place to show how the same is carried on through that space wherein the Christian church shall be visibly in a state of peace and prosperity, viz. from the destruction of Satan's ‹visible kingdom› to Christ's appearing on the clouds of heaven. And here it was proposed, I. to speak of the prosperous state of the church through the bigger part of this period. This has been already done.

II.3 I proposed to speak of the great apostasy there should be towards the close of this period, and how eminently the church should be for a short time threatened by her enemies. And this is what I now come to, and this I shall speak to under three particulars.

-- 488 --

1.4 A little before the end of the world there shall be a very great apostasy, wherein great part of the world shall fall away from Christ and his church. It is said in the Revelation 20:3, that Satan should be cast into the bottomless pit and shut up and have "a seal set upon him,5 that he should deceive the nations no more, till the thousand years should be fulfilled: and that after that he must be loosed" out of his prison for "a little season."6 And accordingly we are told in the Revelation 20:7–8 that "when the thousand years are expired, Satan shall be loosed out of his prison, and should go out to deceive the nations which are in the four quarters of the earth, Gog and Magog."7 Which seems to show as though the apostasy would be very general; the nations of the four quarters of the earth shall [be] deceived. And the number of those that now shall turn enemies to Christ shall [be] vastly great as the army of Gog and Magog is represented in Ezekiel, as 'tis said in the latter part of the Revelation 20:8, that the number of them is as the sand of the sea, and that they went up on the breadth of the earth as though they were an army big enough to reach from one side of the earth to the other.8

Thus after such a happy and glorious season, such a long day of light and holiness, love and peace and joy, now it shall begin again to be a dark time; Satan shall begin to set up his dominion again in the world. This world shall again become9 a scene of darkness and wickedness. The bottomless pit of hell shall be opened, and devils shall come up again out of it, and a dreadful smoke shall ascend to darken the world.1 And the church of Christ, instead of extending to the utmost bounds of the world as it did before, shall be reduced to narrow limits again.2 The world of mankind being continued so long in a state of such great prosperity,3 shall now begin to abuse their prosperity to serve their lust and corruption; this we may learn from Luke 17:26 etc. ["And as it was in the days of Noah.… They did

-- 489 --

eat, they drank, they married wives … they sold, they planted … but the same day … it rained fire and brimstone from heaven.… Even thus shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed"].4 Thus it shall be for a little season. God won't suffer it to continue long because this is not the proper day of the church's trouble; that was ended at the fall of Antichrist, as we have showed already. And therefore a time as this won't continue long.

52.6 Those apostates shall make a great opposition to the church of God, and the church shall seem to be imminently threatened with a sudden and entire overthrow by them. It is said, Satan shall gather them together to battle, as the sand on the sea shore, "and they went up on the breadth of the earth, and compassed the camp of the saints about, and the beloved city";7 so that this beloved city shall seem just ready to be swallowed up by them. For her enemies shall not only have threatened her, but shall actually have gathered together against her; and not only so but shall have besieged her, shall have compassed her about on every side. There is nothing in the prophecy that seems to hold forth as though the church had actually fallen into their hands, as the church formerly had fallen into the hands of Antichrist, to whom it was given "to make war with the saints and overcome them."8 God will never suffer this to be again after the fall of Antichrist, for then "the days of her mourning shall be ended."9 But the church shall seem most imminently threatened1 with utter and sudden destruction.

3.2 Now the state of things will seem most remarkably to call for Christ's immediate appearance to judgment. For then the world shall be filled with the most aggravated wickedness that ever it was. For much the bigger part of the world shall have become visibly wicked, and open enemies to Christ, and their wickedness shall [be] dreadfully aggravated by their apostasy. Before the fall of Antichrist most of the world was full of visibly wicked men; but the bigger part of these are poor heathens that never enjoyed the light of the gospel

-- 490 --

and others were those that [had] been bred up in gross ignorance, in Mohammedan or popish darkness. But these are those that have apostatized from the Christian church and the visible kingdom of Christ in which they enjoyed the great light and privileges of those glorious times of the church, which shall be incomparably greater than the light and privileges that the church of God enjoys now. This apostasy will be most like the apostasy of the devils of any that ever had before been, for the devils3 apostatized and turned enemies to Christ, though they enjoyed the light of heaven; and these will apostatize and turn enemies to him, though they have enjoyed the light and privileges of the glorious times of the church.4 That such should turn open and avowed enemies to Christ, and should seek the ruin of his church, will cry aloud for such immediate vengeance as was executed on the devils when they fell.

The wickedness of the world will remarkably call for Christ's immediate appearing in flaming fire to take vengeance on them,5 because of the way in which they shall manifest their wickedness, which shall be by scoffing and blaspheming at Christ and his holy religion; and particularly [they] will scoff at the notion of Christ's coming to judgment, that the church shall be in expectation of and will warn them of. For now doubtless will be another fulfillment, and the greatest fulfillment, 2 Peter 3:3–4, "Knowing this first, that there shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts, And saying, Where is the promise of his coming? for since the fathers [fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation].6 [They] shall be in no expectation of the coming of Christ in judgment and shall laugh at the notion. They shall trample all such things under foot,7 and shall give up themselves to their lusts,8 or to eat and drink and wallow in sensual delights, as though they were to be here forever.

They shall despise the warnings the church shall give them of the coming of Christ to judgment, as the people of the old world despised what Noah told 'em of the approaching flood, and as the people of

-- 491 --

Sodom did when Lot said to 'em, "The Lord will destroy this city."9 Their wickedness on this account will cry aloud to heaven for Christ's appearing in flaming fire to take vengeance.1 And also because another way that they shall exercise their wickedness will be in their wicked design and violent temper they shall then be engaged in against the holy city of God, against that holy city wherein lately and for so long a time so much of the religion of Christ has been seen. They shall then be about to perpetrate a most horrid design against this church.

And the numerousness of the wicked that shall2 then be is another thing that will especially call ‹for the coming of Christ to judgment›. For the world then will doubtless be exceeding full of people, having continued so long in such a state of great prosperity without such terrible, desolating calamities as wars, pestilences, and the like to diminish them.3 And the most of this world that then will be so populous will be such wicked, contemptuous apostates from God. Undoubtedly that will be a day wherein the world will be by far fuller of wickedness than ever before it was since the foundation of it. And if the wickedness of the old world, when men began to multiply on the earth, called for the world's being destroyed by a deluge of waters, this wickedness will as much call for its being destroyed by a deluge of fire.4

And then the circumstances of the church at that day will also imminently call for the immediate appearing of Christ; for they will be compassed about by their blasphemous, murtherous enemies, just ready to be swallowed up by them. And it will be a most distressing time with the church, excepting the comfort they will have in hope of deliverance from God; for all other help will5 seem to fail. The

-- 492 --

case will be come to the last extremity, and here will be an immediate need that Christ should come to their deliverance. And though the church shall be so imminently threatened, yet so will providence order it, that it shall be preserved till the time approved comes for Christ to appear6 in the glory of his Father with all his holy angels.7 And then will come the time when all the elect shall be gathered in; that work of conversion that has gone from the beginning of the church after the fall, through all these ages, shall be carried on no more. There never shall another soul be converted. Every one of those many millions, whose names were written in the book of life before the foundation of the world,8 shall be brought out; not one soul shall be left. And the mystical body of Christ, which has been growing ever since it first began in the days of Adam, will now be complete as to number of parts, having every one of its members; in this respect the Work of Redemption will be now finished.9 And now the end for which the means of grace1 have been instituted shall be obtained; all that effect that was intended to be accomplished by them shall now be accomplished.

And thus I have shown how the success of Christ's purchase has been accomplished during the Christian church's continuing under means of grace. We have seen what great revolutions there have been and are to be during this space of time, how the great wheels of providence have gone round for the accomplishment of that kind of success of Christ's purchase that consists in the bestowment of grace on the elect; and we are in the prosecution of this subject come to the time when all the wheels have gone round. The course of things in this state of the world is finished, and all things are ripe for Christ's coming to judgment.

You may remember that when I began to discourse on this third proposition, viz. that from the resurrection of Christ ‹to the end of the world the space of time is taken up in bringing about the success or effect of Christ's purchase of redemption›, I observed that the success of Christ's purchase is of two kinds, consisting either in grace

-- 493 --

or glory; and the success consisting in the former of these is to be seen in those works of God that are wrought during those ages that the church is continued under means of grace, and that the success consisting in the latter will chiefly be accomplished at the day2 of judgment. Having already shown that the former kind of success has been accomplished, I come now, in the,

Second3 place, to the latter, viz. that kind of success which is accomplished in the bestowment of glory on the church, which shall chiefly be bestowed at the day of judgment.

And4 I would have mentioned two or three things in the general concerning this kind of success of Christ's purchase.

1.5 How great the success of Christ's purchase is chiefly appears in this: the success of christ's purchase does summarily consist in the salvation of the elect. But this bestowment of glory is eminently called their salvation, Hebrews 9:28, "To those that look for him he shall appear the second time without sin to salvation."6 So it is called redemption, being eminently that wherein the redemption of the church consists: Ephesians 4:30, "sealed unto the day of redemption"; Luke 21:28; 7 and Ephesians 1:14, "redemption of purchased possession."

2.8 All that is before this, while the church is under means of grace, is only to make way for that, to prepare that success that is to be accomplished in the bestowment of glory. The means of grace are to fit for glory, and God's grace itself is bestowed on the elect to make them meet for glory.

93.1 All those glorious things that were brought to pass for the church while under means of grace are but images and shadows of this. So were those glorious things that were accomplished for the church in the days of Constantine the Great, and so is all that glory that is to be accomplished in the glorious times of the church that is to succeed the fall of Antichrist. As great as it is, it is all but a shadow of what will be bestowed at the day of judgment, and therefore as I

-- 494 --

have already often observed, all these preceding glorious events by which God wrought glorious things for his church are spoken of in Scripture as images of Christ's last coming to judgment.

But2 I hasten particularly to show how this kind3 of success of Christ's purchase is accomplished.

1.4 Christ will appear in the glory of his father with all the holy angels coming on the clouds of heaven.5 While the world is thus reveling in their wickedness, and compassing the holy city, about it, just ready to destroy it, and while the church is reduced to such a great strait, then shall the glorious Redeemer appear. He through whom this redemption has all along been carried on,6 he shall appear in the sight of the world, the light of his glory shall break forth. Thus 'tis said, Revelation 20:9.7 The whole world shall immediately have notice of it, and they shall lift up their eyes and behold this wonderful sight. It is said, "every eye shall see him," Revelation 1:7. Christ shall appear, coming in his human nature in that same body that was brought forth in a stable and laid in a manger, and that afterwards was so cruelly used and nailed to the cross.

Men shall now lift up their eyes, and seeing him coming in such majesty and glory as now is to us utterly inconceivable, the glory of the sun in a clear firmament will be but darkness in comparison of it. And all the glorious angels and archangels attending upon, thousand thousands ministering to him, and ten thousand times ten thousand round about him.8 In how different a man9 will he then appear from what he did at his first coming, when he was as a root out of a dry ground, a poor, despised, afflicted man. How different now is his appearance in the midst of those glorious angels, principalities, and powers in heavenly places,1 attending him as his ordinary servants,2

-- 495 --

from what it was when in the midst of a ring of soldiers with his mock robe and crown of thorns to be buffeted and spit upon, or hanging on the cross between two thieves with a multitude of his enemies about him, triumphing over him. This sight will be a most unexpected sight to the wicked world. It will come as a cry at midnight; they shall be taken in the midst of their wickedness; it will give them a dreadful alarm.3 It will at once break up all their revels, their eating and drinking and carousing. It will put a quick end to the design of the great army of the wicked that will then be compassing the camp of the saints about; it will make 'em let drop their weapons out of their hands.

The world, that will then be very full of people most of which will be wicked men, will then be filled with dolorous shrieking and crying, for "all the kindreds of the earth shall wail because of him," Revelation 1:7. And where shall they hide themselves,4 how will the sight of that awful majesty terrify them, when taken in the midst of their wickedness.5 Then they shall see who he is, what kind of a person he is whom they have mocked and scoffed at and whose church they have been endeavoring to overthrow. This sight will change their voice; the voice of their laughter and singing while they are marrying and giving in marriage, and the voice of their scoffing, shall be changed into hideous, yea hellish, yellings.6 Their countenances shall be changed from a show of carnal mirth, haughty pride, and contempt of God's people; it shall put on a show of ghastly terror and amazement, and trembling and chattering of teeth shall seize them.

But with respect to the saints, the church of Christ, it shall be a most joyful and glorious sight to them. For this sight will at once deliver them from all fear of their enemies that were before compassing them about, just ready to swallow them. Deliverance shall come in their extremity; the glorious captain of their salvation7 shall appear for them8 at a time when no other help appeared. Then shall they lift up their heads, and see their redemption drawing nigh, Luke 21:28. And thus Christ will appear with infinite might. Then

-- 496 --

yet at the same time they shall see infinite love in his countenance to them. And thus to see their redeemer coming in the clouds of heaven will fill their hearts full of gladness. Their countenances also shall be changed, but not as the countenances of the wicked will be, but shall be changed from being sorrowful to be exceeding joyful and triumphant. And now that Work of Redemption will be finished in another respect, viz. that the whole church shall be completely and eternally freed from all persecution and molestation from wicked men and devils.9

2.1 The last trumpet shall sound and the dead shall be raised and the living changed.2 God sent forth his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, to gather together his elect from the four corners of the earth in a mystical sense before the destruction of Jerusalem, i.e. he sent forth the apostles and others to preach the gospel all over the world. And so in a mystical sense the great trumpet was blown at the beginning of the glorious times of the church. But now the great trumpet is blown in a more literal sense, with a mighty sound that shall shake the earth. There will3 be a great signal given by a mighty sound made, that is called the voice of the archangel, as being the angel of greatest strength, 1 Thessalonians 4:16, "For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with a trump of God."

On the sound of the great trumpet, the dead shall be raised everywhere. Now the number of the dead is very great; how many has death cut down for so long a time as since the world has stood. But then the number will be much greater, after the world has stood so much longer time; and through most of the remaining time will doubtless be much fuller of inhabitants than ever it has been. All these shall now rise from the dead. The graves shall be opened everywhere, in all parts of the world, and the sea shall give up the innumerable dead that are in it, Revelation 20:13. And now all the inhabitants that ever have been upon the face of the earth, from the beginning of the world to that time, shall all appear upon earth at once. All that ever have been of the church of God in all ages: Adam and Eve, the first parents of mankind; and Abel, and Seth, and Methuselah, and all the saints that were their contemporaries; and Noah; and

-- 497 --

Abraham; and Isaac; and Jacob;4 and the prophets of Israel; and the saints in the time of Antiochus Epiphanes, and all that were in the church in their times; and all the holy apostles of Jesus Christ, and all the saints of their times; and all the holy martyrs under the ten heathen persecutions; and all that belonged to the church in its wilderness state during the dark times of Antichrist; and all the holy martyrs that have suffered under the cruelty of the popish persecutions; and all the saints of the present time; and all the saints that are here in this assembly among the rest; and all that shall be from hence to the end of the world.

And now also all the enemies of the church that have been, or shall be in all the ages of the world, shall then appear upon the face of the earth again: all the wicked killed in the flood; and the multitudes that died all over the world among God's professing people or others; all that died in all heathen nations before Christ; and all wicked heathens, and Jews, and Mohammedans, and papists that lived [and] died since. All shall come up together; sinners of all sorts: demure hypocrites—those that have the fairest and best outside, and openly profane drunkards, whoremasters; heretics, deists, and all cruel persecutors,5 and all that have died or shall die in sin amongst us.

And at the same time that the dead are raised, the living shall be changed. The bodies of the wicked that shall be then living shall be so changed as to fit 'em for eternal torment without corruption, and the bodies of all the living saints shall be changed to be like Christ's glorious body, 1 Corinthians 15:51–53 ["We shall all be changed.… The dead shall be raised incorruptible.… For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality"]. Then the bodies of the saints [shall] be so changed as to render [them] forever uncapable of any more pain, or affliction, or uneasiness, and all that dullness and heavy-moldedness, and all that deformity that their bodies before had; and [they] shall ever put on strength, and beauty, and activity, and incorruptible, unfading glory. And in such glory shall the bodies of all the risen saints appear.

And now the Work of Redemption shall be finished in another respect, viz. that all the elect shall now be actually redeemed in both body and soul. Before this the Work of Redemption as to its actual success was but incomplete and imperfect, for only the souls of the

-- 498 --

redeemed were actually saved and glorified, excepting in some few instances.6 But now all the bodies of the saints shall be saved and glorified together, all the elect shall be glorified in the whole man, and the soul and body in union one with another.

3.7 Now shall the whole church of saints be caught up in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air, and all wicked men and devils shall be arraigned before the judgment seat.8 When the dead saints are raised, then the whole church, consisting of all the elect through all ages, will be standing on the face of the earth together, at least excepting those few whose bodies were glorified before; and then they shall all mount up as with wings in the air to go and meet Christ. For it seems that Christ when he comes to judgment, won't come quite down to the ground, but his throne will be fixed in the air in the region of the clouds, whence he may be seen by all that vast multitude that shall be gathered before him. And the church of saints therefore shall be taken up off from the earth to ascend up to their savior. Thus the Apostle tells us that when the dead in9 Christ are raised and the living changed, then those "which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them to meet the Lord in the air, and so shall we be ever with the Lord," 1 Thessalonians 4:16–17.1 What a wonderful sight will this be when all the many millions of saints are seen thus mounting up from all parts of the world.

Then shall the Work of Redemption be finished in another respect: then the whole church shall be perfectly and forever delivered from this present evil world, forever forsake this cursed ground. They shall take their everlasting leave of this earth where they have been strangers, and that has been for the most part such a scene of their trouble and sorrow, where the devil for the most part has reigned as god, and has greatly molested them, and which has been a scene of wickedness and abomination, where Christ their Lord has been cruelly used, and where they have been so hated, and reproached, and persecuted, from age to age through most of the ages of the world. They shall leave it under foot to go to Christ, and never shall set foot on it again. And then shall be an everlasting separation made between them and

-- 499 --

wicked men. Before they were mixed together, and now all become visible.

Then shall all the church be seen flocking together in the air to the place where Christ shall have fixed his throne,2 coming from the east, and west, and north, and south, to the right hand of Christ.3 What a mighty cloud of them will there be when all that ever have been of the church of God, all that were before Christ, all that multitude of saints that were in the apostles' times, and all that were in the days of Constantine the Great, and all that were before and since the Reformation, and also all that great multitude of saints that shall be in all the glorious times of the church, when the whole earth shall for so many generations be full of saints, and also all that shall then be found living when Christ come, I say, what a cloud of them will there be when all these are seen flocking together in the region of the clouds at the right hand of Christ.

And then also will the Work of Redemption be finished in another respect, viz. that now the church shall all be gathered together. They all belonged to one society before, but yet were greatly separated with respect to the place of their habitation, some in heaven and some on earth. And those that were on earth were separated one from another, many of them by wide oceans and vast continents. But now they shall all be gathered4 together, never to be separated any more. And not only shall all the members of the church now be gathered together, but all shall be gathered unto their head, into his immediate glorious presence, never to be separated from him any more; this never came to pass till now.

At the same time all wicked men and devils shall be brought before the judgment seat of Christ, on the left hand, on the earth, and not in the air as the saints will be.5 The devil, that old serpent, shall now be dragged up out of hell. He that first procured the fall and misery of mankind, and has so set himself against his redemption, and has all along shown himself such an inveterate enemy to the Redeemer, now he shall never more have anything to do when the church of God [is gathered together. He shall not]6 be suffered in the least to afflict

-- 500 --

or molest any of them any more forever. Instead of that, now he must be judged and receive the due reward of his deeds. Now is come the time which he has always dreaded and trembled at the thought [of], the time wherein he must be judged and receive his full punishment. He that by his temptation maliciously procured Christ's crucifixion, and triumphed upon it as though he had got7 the victory, now he shall see the consequence of the death of Christ that he procured; for Christ's coming to judge him in his human nature is the consequence of it, for Christ obtained and purchased this glory to himself by that death. Now must he stand before that same Jesus whose death he procured to be judged, condemned, and eternally destroyed by him. If Satan, the prince of hell, trembles at the thought of it thousands of years beforehand, how much more will he tremble as proud and as stubborn as he is when he comes to stand at Christ's bar.8

Then shall he also stand at the bar of the saints that he has so hated and afflicted and molested, for the saints shall judge him with Christ, 1 Corinthians 6:3, "Know ye not that we shall judge angels?" Now shall he be, as it were, subdued under the church's feet, agreeable to Romans 16:20. Satan when he first tempted our first parents to fall, deceitfully and lyingly told them that they should be as gods; but little did he think that the consequence should be that they should indeed and be so much as gods as to be assessors with God, to judge. How much less did he think that9 the consequence would be that one of the nature that he then tempted, one of the posterity of those persons that he tempted, should actually be united to God so as to be in the same person with one that was God; and that as God he should judge the world, and that he must stand trembling and astonished before his judgment seat. But thus it is, all the devils of hell, that have so long opposed Christ and his kingdom, shall now at last stand in utmost reversal and horror before Christ and his church, who shall appear in glory to condemn them.

Now also shall all Christ's other enemies be brought to appear before him. Now shall wicked, proud scribes and Pharisees, that had such a malignant hatred of Christ while in his state of humiliation, and that persecuted Christ to death, those before whose judgment seat Christ was once called and stood as a poor, abject malefactor at their bar, and those that mocked him and buffeted him and spit in

-- 501 --

his face: now shall they see Christ in his glory, as Christ forewarned them in the time of it, Matthew 26:64–65 ["Hereafter shall ye see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of power, and coming in the clouds of heaven. Then the high priest rent his clothes"].1 Then Christ was before their judgment seat, but now it is their turn. They shall stand before his judgment seat with inconceivable horror and amazement, with ghastly countenances, and quaking limbs, and chattering teeth, and knees smiting one against another.

Now also shall all the cruel enemies and persecutors of the church that have been in all ages come in sight together. Pharaoh and the Egyptians, Antiochus Epiphanes, persecuting scribes and Pharisees, persecuting heathen emperors, Julian the Apostate, cruel persecuting popes and papists, and Gog and Magog, shall all appear at once. They, and the saints that have in every age been persecuted by 'em, shall come in sight one of another, and must confront one another now before the great judge. And now shall the saints on their glorious thrones be made the judges of those unjust kings and rulers that have before judged and condemned them, and cruelly put 'em to death. Even shall2 those persecutors behold the glory which they are arrived at, that they before so despised and so cruelly used. And now Christ will make those holy martyrs, as it were, to come and set their feet on the necks of their persecutors.3 They shall be made their footstool.4 Thus wonderfully will the face of things be altered from what used to be in the former times of the world; now will all things be coming to rights.5

-- 502 --

1SERMON TWENTY-NINE Aug. 17392
[For the moth shall eat them up like a garment, and the worm shall eat them like wool: but my righteousness shall be for ever, and my salvation from generation to generation.] Isaiah 51:8
DOCTRINE
[The Work of Redemption is a work that God carries on from the fall of man to the end of the world.]
PROPOSITION
[That the space of time from the end of Christ's humiliation to the end of the world is all taken up in bringing about the great effect or success of Christ's purchase.]

WE were last showing how the second sort of success of Christ's purchase is accomplished, viz. that which consists in the bestowment of glory, which is chiefly at the day of judgment. And concerning the great events that appertain to this day, several things have already been observed: viz. 1. that Christ will appear in the glory of his Father with all his holy angels coming in the clouds of heaven; 2. that the last trumpet shall sound, and the dead raised, and the living changed; 3. that the whole church of saints shall mount up as with wings, being caught up in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air, and so gather together in the air at the place where Christ has fixed his throne, at his right hand. And that at the same time all wicked men and devils

-- 503 --

shall be arraigned before the judgment seat below on the earth, at Christ's left hand.

I now proceed further to set forth the great transactions of that day. And in the,

Fourth3 place, the righteousness of the church shall be manifested and all the wickedness of their enemies shall be brought4 to light. Those saints that had been the subjects of hatred, reproach, and contempt in this world, and were reviled and condemned by their persecutors without a cause, shall now be fully vindicated.5 They shall now appear clothed with the glorious robe of Christ's righteousness.6 It shall be most manifest before the world that that righteousness is theirs, and they shall, as it were, gloriously shine forth in it. And then also shall their inherent holiness be made manifest, all their good works be brought to light. The good things they did in secret shall now be manifested openly.7 These holy ones of God that had been treated as though they were the filth and offscouring of the earth, as though they were not fit to live upon earth, as worse than beasts and like devils, shall now when things shall appear as they are, appear to have been those that have been the excellent of the earth.8 Now God will bring forth their righteousness as the light and their judgment as the noonday.9

1And now it shall appear who were those wicked persons that were not fit to live, when all the wickedness of the enemies of Christ and his church—their pride, their malice, their cruelty, their hatred of true religion—shall be set forth in all the horrid acts of it with all its aggravations, in its proper colors. And now the righteous may be heard before this great judge, that could not be heard before those unjust judges. Now they shall declare their cause, and shall rise up in judgment against their persecutors, and shall declare how they have been treated by them. And all the wickedness of the wicked of the whole world shall now be brought to light, all their secret wickedness, and their very hearts shall ‹be› opened to view and, as it were,

-- 504 --

turned inside out before the bright light of that great day. And things that have been spoken in the ear or closet and done in the dark, shall be manifested in the light and proclaimed before all angels and men that are or ever were or will be.

25.3 The sentence shall be pronounced on the righteous and the wicked. Christ, the glorious judge, shall pass that blessed sentence on the church at his right hand, "Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit [the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world]."4 This sentence shall be pronounced with infinite love, and the voice will be most sweet, causing every heart to overflow with joy. Thus Christ will pronounce a sentence of justification on thousands and millions that have before had a sentence of condemnation passed on 'em by their persecuting rulers. He will thus put honor upon those that have been before despised, he will own them for his5 and will, as it were, put a crown of glory upon their heads before the world.6 And then shall they shine forth as the sun with Jesus Christ in glory, and joy in the sight of all their enemies.7 And then shall the sentence of condemnation be passed on the wicked, "Depart from me, ye cursed, into [everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels]."8 Thus shall the church's enemies be condemned, in which sentence of condemnation the holy martyrs that have suffered from them shall concur. When the9 words of this sentence are pronounced, they will strike every heart of those at the left hand with immense horror and amazement; every syllable of it will be more terrible than a stream of lightning through their hearts.
